Your Step 3d re-gate PASSED; this gates only what changed since, plus one thing that changed BENEATH that PASS.

THE MAIN EVENT — A FIGURE YOU PASSED HAS CHANGED, AND IT IS THE FIFTH FIRING OF THIS RUN'S OWN ANTI-PATTERN. You dispatched N2 as a one-clause scoping fix: change 'Three such deaths are on record' to 'Three such deaths of a dispatched agent holding an open handoff'. DOC-UPDATER applied the scope and then re-derived the count inside it, and reports the scoped sentence is FALSE — there are FOUR. It cites `handoffs/registry.json:729`, run WF02-REQ038-20260817: 'One infra-terminated CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR dispatch (connection error mid-work, zero commits, cleanly re-dispatched from scratch without incrementing rework_count — matching the WF02-REQ027-20260816 step_2d_infra_restart precedent)'. Same class, same treatment as a row already in your table. It was invisible to YOUR Step 3d sweep because the dead dispatch committed nothing: no handoff file, no orchestrator.log line, only one clause inside a run-level note. §4.1's table now carries four rows and reads 'Four incidents, three different treatments'.

GATE IT PROPERLY, because it is exactly the shape this whole run keeps re-encountering: your Step 3d pass re-derived the death COUNT inside the class you had inherited, and the class was too narrow. Re-derive the FOURTH row from the source, and — more important — **re-derive the CLASS BOUNDARY itself.** Do not simply confirm WF02-REQ038 exists. Ask what search would have found it, run that search, and report whether it finds a FIFTH. Specifically: the finding proves that an agent death can leave no handoff file, no log line, and no artefact except prose inside a run-level `note` or `last_known_step`, so a sweep over `handoffs/**/step-*.json` structurally cannot see it. Sweep `registry.json`'s prose fields and `orchestrator.log` on their own terms. If the true count is not four, say so and give the number with its evidence.

ALSO GATE:

(1) THE SEVENTH MEMBER — a genuine self-contradiction DOC-UPDATER correctly declined to resolve alone, since it is a schema decision your re-gate had already passed. §4.1(b) says the object has 'all six members below' and gives a six-row table. The backfilled ISS-0109 file now carries SEVEN, the extra being `backfill_note`. So the one file the field exists to enumerate does not conform to the field's own stated shape, and a linter built from (b) — which §4.1(b) explicitly anticipates, and which is filed as ISS-0191 — would reject it. Rule on which is right: (a) 'six' is a required MINIMUM and (b)'s wording should say so, permitting additional members; (b) `backfill_note` should be a defined seventh member; (c) `backfill_note` does not belong and its content should fold into an existing member such as `reason` or `evidence`. This is the same failure shape as `docs/anti-patterns.md`'s 'Validating a design's type table for well-formedness instead of against its own normative section' — a normative table and a real instance disagreeing — so hold it to that standard: check the table against the actual file, member by member, not the table on its own.

(2) THE BACKFILL'S FIDELITY. DOC-UPDATER reports a parsed-structure diff showing 14 removed paths all under /orch_reconstruction/, 18 added all under /not_agent_attested/, zero changed values on common paths, zero values present-before-and-now-gone, and that the two \uXXXX escapes are byte-identical. Verify that independently — this is the one file in the repo whose whole point is that a reconstruction stays distinguishable from a measurement, so an edit that silently altered an assertion inside it would be the worst possible outcome of this run. Confirm no factual assertion was added, removed or reworded, and that the six (or seven) members carry the same content the old key did. Also confirm the rename did not leave a dangling reference: DOC-UPDATER reports all five `orch_reconstruction` mentions were inside HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and that four other sentences had to be updated or they would have become false — check those four read correctly now.

(3) N1, N3, N4 CLOSED, AND TWO REPORTED DIVERGENCES FROM YOUR OWN FINDINGS. DOC-UPDATER re-derived rather than adopting your figures and diverges twice: on N1 it finds top-level `next_action` in SIX files where your finding said five (noting your own enumeration listed six while saying five), and on N3 it finds 46 handoffs created 2026-08-21 with 42 predating commit 131aba9 where you said 45/43, attributing the gap to `step-03b` landing 47 seconds after the commit and to a local-time-vs-UTC comparison. Adjudicate both by measuring. Whichever way they go, one of the two records is wrong and the corpus should not keep the wrong one.

(4) THE TWO ANTI-PATTERNS ENTRIES. `docs/anti-patterns.md` grew 968 → 1070 lines, +102/-0, heading diff `21a22,23` only — ORCH confirms the file did not shrink. Gate the CONTENT: does the first entry state a transferable MECHANISM rather than a narrative of who erred, does it correctly identify the gate as a carrier, and does it cross-link both 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' and core-directives.md's 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'? DOC-UPDATER reports finding a FIFTH firing while writing it — that your Step 3d re-derived the count inside an inherited class — which is the same finding as the main event above; check the entry states it accurately and without overstating your error. The second entry covers overwriting a dispatched `task` block. Both must be proportionate: an anti-patterns entry that reads as an indictment rather than a procedure is less likely to be followed.

(5) §3's NEW `task` ROW. Added per item (7) of the ride-along, citing the 6,290→156-character incident. Check it is proportionate to a MINOR gap, that it correctly says ORCH writes `task` and the receiving agent never modifies it, that it directs a receiving agent who believes its task is wrong to §1.1's report-in-result.issues path rather than to editing, and that its Exception column is empty — there is no §4.1 exception for `task`.

(6) NOTHING PREVIOUSLY PASSING WAS DISTURBED. 89 changed lines in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md is large for four one-clause fixes plus two small additions, and the rename touched five call sites. Confirm §4.1(a), (c), (d), §3's other rows, §2's fence and ORCHESTRATOR.md §5/§7.2 are unchanged in substance — prefer a hash or a targeted diff over reading by eye, as you did at Step 3d.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL. Every finding here is expected to be a text correction; if you FAIL, it is rework iteration 2 of 3 and you must say so and name each unclosed item. If you PASS, state the budget standing. NOTE THAT ITEM (1) MAY REQUIRE A TEXT CHANGE WHICHEVER WAY YOU RULE — a PASS that leaves §4.1(b) saying 'six' while the enumerated file carries seven is not a coherent verdict, so rule and route rather than noting it. You may NOT edit any file under docs/ or another run's handoff. Write only this handoff. Report anything needing an id in result.issues — ORCH allocates.

result.summary:
FINAL GATE on 0bbb2cc: FAIL, rework iteration 2 of 3 (max_rework 3; one iteration remains after this one). Every finding is a text correction inside docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4.1; no artefact is wrong, no measurement committed in 0bbb2cc is wrong, and the ISS-0109 backfill is clean. Two items block.

MAIN EVENT -- THE FOURTH DEATH IS REAL; THE CLASS BOUNDARY IS NOT YET DECIDABLE. Re-derived the fourth row from source, not from the report: handoffs/registry.json /runs/29/note (WF02-REQ038-20260817) carries verbatim 'One infra-terminated CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR dispatch (connection error mid-work, zero commits, cleanly re-dispatched from scratch without incrementing rework_count -- matching the WF02-REQ027-20260816 step_2d_infra_restart precedent).' Confirmed invisible to a handoff-file sweep: handoffs/WF02-REQ038-20260817/ holds no artefact of that dead dispatch, and a regex sweep of handoffs/orchestrator.log returns no WF02-REQ038 death line. DOC-UPDATER is right; my Step 3d sweep was structurally blind to it. Four rows, three treatments: CORRECT AS WRITTEN.

I then re-derived the CLASS BOUNDARY rather than the count, as dispatched. Method: a python walk over EVERY string leaf of registry.json (not just `note`), matching a termination-vocabulary regex -- 46 raw hits, 43 unique, each printed with its JSON path and run id -- plus an independent grep of orchestrator.log on its own terms. Both commands are quoted below. RESULT: no fifth member of the table's class. That nil result is a measured finding, not an assumption. But the same sweep surfaces a SECOND excluded abnormal termination that section 4.1 neither mentions nor can currently adjudicate: WF02-REQ019-20260816. registry.json /runs/2/note reads 'This run was interrupted mid-pipeline when the host process exited AFTER STEP 4 DISPATCH, then resumed in a later session from Step 4 onward', and orchestrator.log:50 reads 'Committed and pushed the ORPHANED STEP 4 DISPATCH log line (commit 2682e06).' A dispatch had been issued and the host died; Step 4 was then re-dispatched to a fresh TEST-RUNNER -- the identical treatment the table records for WF02-REQ027 and WF02-REQ038. So it is IN-class under the table's own treatment pattern, and OUT-of-class under the test the section applies to WF02-REQ025 ('holding no agent handoff ... no result was ever left for a second party to complete'), since no pre-crash handoff file survives and the re-dispatch's own task text says the prior session 'was interrupted before Step 4 could run'. The corpus cannot settle it, because the section states a class NAME but no decidable MEMBERSHIP TEST -- and it presents its exclusion set as closed at one member. That is this run's own anti-pattern firing a SIXTH time, one level up again: the exclusion set was enumerated by the same handoff-file-shaped sweep that missed WF02-REQ038. The defect is the undecidable boundary, not the count.

ITEM (1) RULED -- OPTION (b). Verified member by member against the actual file rather than reading the table alone: the marker carries seven members (reconstructed_by, reconstructed_at, reason, fields_written, evidence, not_verifiable_after_the_fact, backfill_note) while HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:471 says 'an object with all six members below' over a six-row table. The six required ones each match the file exactly, including fields_written holding precisely the table's example value. Rejected (a) 'six is a minimum': it converts a closed enumeration into an open one and costs ISS-0191's linter the ability to reject a junk or misspelled member, which is most of the field's value. Rejected (c) 'fold into reason': `reason` asserts why the RESULT is not agent-attested (ELIXIR-DEV died on an API error), while `backfill_note` asserts why this MARKER was applied retroactively -- merging them collapses exactly the reconstruction-vs-measurement distinction, in the one file whose entire purpose is preserving it. Ruled (b): `backfill_note` becomes a defined seventh member, OPTIONAL, admissible only on a file amended under 4.1(b)'s single named exception, which is now spent. Routed as BLOCKER-1 with the exact text change, so the verdict does not leave (b) contradicting the file it enumerates.

ITEM (2) -- BACKFILL FIDELITY INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, CLEAN. Reproduced the parsed-structure diff from the git objects at 4101459 and 0bbb2cc rather than trusting the report: 14 removed paths ALL under /orch_reconstruction/, 18 added ALL under /not_agent_attested/, ZERO changed values on common paths, and ZERO old leaf values absent from the new file. Exactly four genuinely new leaf values: 'status', 'completed_at', 'result' (the fields_written declaration, which section 3 independently establishes ORCH did write and did not declare) and the backfill_note text. No factual assertion was added, removed or reworded: all nine commands_run entries and both not_verifiable_after_the_fact entries carry over verbatim under the new member names. Non-ASCII: both revisions contain exactly two escapes, U+26A0 and U+FE0F, byte-identical, and zero literal non-ASCII characters. The rename left no dangling reference -- all four dependent sentences read correctly now (section 3's completed_at breach paragraph, the new 'as improvised' note, 4.1(b)'s backfill paragraph, 4.1(c)'s worked-example pointer); each names the current key and parenthesises the historical one, so none became false. PASS.

ITEM (3) -- BOTH DIVERGENCES ADJUDICATED BY MEASUREMENT. DOC-UPDATER is right both times and MY OWN STEP 3D RECORD IS THE WRONG ONE. N1: json.load over all 550 handoff files at 0bbb2cc excluding registry.json (0 unparseable) finds a top-level `next_action` in SIX files, enumerated below -- not five. My Step 3d finding said five while its own enumeration listed six, which is the figure-vs-parenthetical mismatch the new anti-patterns entry warns about, committed by the gate whose predecessor prompted the warning. N3: git show -s 131aba9 gives committer date 2026-08-21T12:13:08+05:00 = 07:13:08Z; 46 files carry a 2026-08-21 created_at and exactly 42 predate that instant, 4 do not -- and the earliest of those four is step-03b-reviewer-gate.json at 07:13:55Z, 47 seconds after the commit, precisely the cause DOC-UPDATER names. My 45/43 was wrong. THE COMMITTED TEXT IS CORRECT IN BOTH PLACES and must not be touched; the wrong record is handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03d-reviewer-regate.json. It is a COMPLETED, committed, attested result block and I have not edited it -- correcting it in place is the precise act this run's own amendment prohibits. Filed as a MINOR for ORCH to route as an appended correction, per the WF02-REQ038 precedent of a postscript rather than a silent rewrite of a run's own earlier prose.

ITEM (4) -- BOTH ANTI-PATTERNS ENTRIES PASS ON CONTENT. Entry 1, 'Re-deriving the count while inheriting the unit being counted'. MECHANISM-VS-NARRATIVE: PASS -- the title is the mechanism, the four-step trace is evidence with each step cited to its handoff file rather than a narrative of who erred, and 'Why it is easy to miss' plus five procedural correctives transfer to any category-shaped claim. GATE-AS-CARRIER: PASS, and this is the entry's real contribution -- it states plainly that in every prior instance the carrier was a producer, that here 'the validator did re-derive, and propagated the error anyway', and why a gate is MORE exposed than a producer ('checking a proposition tends to mean testing its predicate, not its subject'). CROSS-LINKS: PASS, both verified present at their targets -- docs/anti-patterns.md:581 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' and docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md:109 'Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about'. The fifth-firing paragraph describes my Step 3d accurately and without overstating it: it credits the independent re-derivation, names the inherited class boundary as the fault, and gives the structural reason. Entry 2, the task block: PASS, and its two figures reproduce exactly -- commit 8f724cc carries a 156-character task.description and 23e6c26 restores 6,290. Proportionate: it says outright 'Nothing about the step's verdict or evidence was affected ... it should not be reported as more than that', and 'Why it happens' explains the edit as tidying rather than malpractice. Its fourth corrective, commit the handoff at dispatch, is the only one that would have prevented the loss outright and is worth adopting as a rule.

ITEM (5) -- SECTION 3'S NEW `task` ROW PASSES ALL FOUR CRITERIA. Proportionate to a MINOR gap: one table row plus one paragraph that leads with the rule and ends by scoping the damage ('The step's verdict and evidence were unaffected; what was nearly lost was the record of what had been asked'). Ownership: 'ORCH only -- it is the dispatch itself, and the receiving agent never modifies it'. Redress path: 'says so in `result.issues` (per section 1.1) and leaves the block alone; ORCH is the only role that can re-dispatch' -- and section 1.1 genuinely carries that path at line 51, so the pointer resolves. Exception column: an em-dash, empty, correct -- 4.1 was not widened to invent an exception for `task`. Also correct and easy to miss: the following heading was updated from 'Why the last two rows exist' to 'Why the `status` and `result` rows exist', which the new sixth row would otherwise have falsified.

ITEM (6) -- NOTHING PREVIOUSLY PASSING WAS DISTURBED, CONFIRMED BY HASH RATHER THAN BY EYE. Split both revisions of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md on headings and compared sha256 per section. BYTE-IDENTICAL: preamble, section 1, section 1.1, SECTION 2 INCLUDING ITS SCHEMA FENCE (a8d9b1e2285c on both sides), the worked-result examples, section 4, 4.1(a) (b07daa4130de), 4.1(d) (83c9c807d668), sections 5, 6, 7, and the enforcement note. CHANGED: section 3, the 4.1 preamble, 4.1(b), 4.1(c) -- all four expected. 4.1(c)'s only hunk is the worked-example pointer rename, so (c) is substantively unchanged as required. ORCHESTRATOR.md is absent from git diff --stat 4101459 0bbb2cc entirely, so its sections 5 and 7.2 are untouched. Separately re-derived section 3's own new arithmetic and it holds exactly: 26 occurrences across 13 files = 4 ad-hoc-repair keys + 6 misplaced next_action + 1 gate_history + 15 foreign-schema keys (8 in WF02-REQ059's step-00-git-setup.json, 7 in WF02-REQ060's).

COMMANDS QUOTED. (a) Fourth row and class boundary: python walk of every string leaf of handoffs/registry.json against re.compile(r'terminat|died|death|kill|API error|connection error|session limit|power outage|crash|abnormal|interrupt|resum|mid-work|mid-run|exited|outage', re.I) -> 46 hits / 43 unique across 12 runs; and grep -nEi 'died|death|terminated|API error|connection error|session limit|power outage|host (process )?(exited|interrupt)|abnormal|orphaned|RESUME \|' handoffs/orchestrator.log -> 26 lines, of which the only agent-death lines are :223 (WF02-REQ027), :297 (WF02-REQ025, ORCH's own session, already excluded by the text) and :50 (WF02-REQ019, the boundary case above). WF02-REQ038 appears in NEITHER, confirming prose-only recording. (b) Divergences: json.load over git ls-tree -r --name-only 0bbb2cc handoffs/ minus registry.json = 550 files, 0 unparseable; top-level next_action in WF02-REQ033/step-01-code-designer, WF02-REQ051/step-05-release-validator, WF02-REQ051/step-06-doc-updater, WF03-ISS0047/step-02-code-designer, WF03-ISS0047/step-04-test-designer, WF03-ISS0047/step-05-issue-fixer = 6. (c) Fidelity: parsed-structure diff of git show 4101459:<file> vs git show 0bbb2cc:<file>. (d) Item 6: per-section sha256 of both revisions.
